findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping in document lookups
findings.body: When tenants share the database, a caller can request another tenant's known document ID because `getDocument` still receives `ctx.tenantId`, but the changed lookup no longer includes it. This regresses the prior authorization boundary and can return cross-tenant data.

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant filtering in document lookups
findings.body:
`ctx.tenantId` is now ignored, so a tenant requesting a known document ID can retrieve a document belonging to another tenant from a shared database. Duplicate document IDs can also return the wrong tenant’s record.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the exported cache module
findings.body:
Deleting `src/cache.ts` breaks compilation or module resolution for every existing consumer importing `readCached`, despite the PR’s contract-preservation requirement.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping to prevent cross-tenant document access
findings.body:
Any tenant that supplies a document ID belonging to another tenant can retrieve it when tenants share the database, because the lookup no longer constrains `tenantId`. This bypasses the prior tenant authorization boundary and exposes cross-tenant data.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore the tenant predicate to bound document queries
findings.body:
When document IDs are tenant-local, a common ID can match one record per tenant. `db.find({ documentId })` therefore materializes and transfers O(number of tenants) records per request instead of one, causing database I/O, memory, and latency to grow with tenant count.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
